unresolvedReferences.description: The English gives 553 for Datong 17; external chronology gives 551, consistent with Wendi's death; repaired.
The legendary boy's age of ten is not converted. The she-wolf and the gods of summer and winter are not human. The ten sons, ten wives, and seventeen brothers are undifferentiated plurals.
The neighboring king (彼王) is not named and is not made a person.
Tumen's wife styled Kehedun may be Princess Changle, but the text does not say so; she has a separate record.
Units s0381-s0385 sit out of sequence in the packet and are treated as written. 阿那瑰 and 阿那瓌 are kept as written.
太祖 is identified externally as Yuwen Tai.
'Three years' names no reign; the year is left unconverted.
Units s0063-s0067 are split around manuscript lacunae and emendations (沒, 勒); they are treated as written.
Ta-bo's 'two southern sons' refers figuratively to the Zhou and Qi rulers; no people are created.

The Qi ruler is identified externally as Gao Zhan. Taizu = Yuwen Tai, Hu = Yuwen Hu, Chun = Yuwen Chun, and Gaozu = Emperor Wu (Yuwen Yong) are also external identifications. Hou-jin's death date (572) is external.
The English renders 'Yang Jian' in both s0104 and s0122 for 楊薦; he is a different person from the Sui founder 楊堅.
Units s0386-s0396 (Ta-bo's later reign) sit before s0135 in the packet and are treated as written.
高祖 and 帝 in s0390 are the same emperor (Wudi died in 578); the English wrongly suggests two people.
The emperor in Daxiang 1-2 may be Xuandi or Jingdi (Xuandi abdicated in 579 but kept power until 580); the record is marked uncertain.
In s0135 the English opening 'Tuyuhun' refers to the polity; the Chinese names the founder as Murong Hui's elder half-brother. The s0139 clan name is not a mention of the person.
s0163-s0165 are split around a lacuna (駿); treated as written.
s0199-s0201 are split around a lacuna (豎); the son is linked as 堅 only.
Mu-han Qaghan is Hou-jin of earlier chunks. Kua-lu's 'wife and children' (妻子) in s0172 are not individuated.
All Tuyuhun founder-line and Hexi/Gaochang ruler dates are external.
s0247-s0249 are split around the emended 封; the base text 張軌所討 means Zhang Gui attacked Long Xi, but the English says he enfeoffed him. Repaired in s0249.
The Gaochang king of Wucheng 1 and Baoding and the kings of Karasahr and Kucha are unnamed and are not made people. The Dukes of Jiaohe and Tiandi in s0205 are generic offices.
The Chinese 焉支 here stands for 焉耆 (Karasahr).
The Shanshan king who fled under Taiwu is unnamed and is a different person from the Datong 8 king.
Piluzhan is an undated legendary arhat. The Khotan king he served, the pratyekabuddha, and the unnamed kings of Khotan, the Hephthalites, Sogdia, Parthia, and Persia are not made people.
Persian court terms (翳囋, 防步率, 殺野) and offices (s0326-s0330) are titles, not individuals.
s0290-s0292 and s0353-s0355 are split around lacunae and emendations; treated as written.
The appraising historian (史臣) is unnamed and is not made a person.
秩宗 and 護軍 refer by office to earlier advisers, probably Yan You and Ban Gu from s0358, but the identification is uncertain and no people are created.
金行…水運 are dynastic-phase terms; the English 'Jin through Sui' is an interpretation and is left unrepaired. s0361-s0363 and s0370-s0372 are split around lacunae.
